checks.title: Transaction group
checks.detail: Opened ${var.transaction}, the transaction group that stood out.

checks.title: Trace path
checks.detail: Followed one representative trace through the request.

answer.evidence: The representative APM trace connects ${truth.finding} to ${truth.scope}.

goals.title: Select the affected service context
goals.concept: APM service and environment filters define the RED metrics and samples being compared.
goals.narration: Open the service the report is about in APM.
goals.reasoning: Service context prevents unrelated traces from entering the comparison.
goals.evidence: The service page shows scenario transactions.

demonstration.narration: I'll open ${var.service} in APM to see the latency and failures for the service in this report.
demonstration.reasoning: The APM inventory combines many services. Selecting ${var.service} prevents unrelated traces from entering the comparison and gives us the correct service context.
demonstration.evidence: The service page now shows transactions for ${var.service}. This establishes where to investigate; the transaction and trace details still need inspection.

hints: Start from the service the report names.
Select ${var.service}; Show me can navigate there.

drifts.note: You opened ${action.value}; the report is about a different service.

goals.title: Open the affected transaction group
goals.concept: Transaction groups aggregate requests with the same operation so their latency and failure distribution can be compared.
goals.narration: Open the transaction group whose latency or failures stand out.
goals.reasoning: The group connects the service-level symptom to representative request samples.
goals.evidence: The transaction detail view shows samples for the affected operation.

demonstration.narration: I'll open the transaction group whose latency or failures stand out, to narrow the question to one operation.
demonstration.reasoning: Service-wide metrics combine different operations. One transaction group narrows the question to comparable requests.
demonstration.evidence: The ${var.transaction} group now shows its latency distribution and request samples. Choose a sample to follow one request end to end.

hints: Find the operation behind the report in the service's transaction table.
Sort the table by latency or failure rate and open the group that stands out.
Open ${var.transaction}; Show me can open it.

drifts.note: You opened ${action.value}; check whether that operation is the one whose latency or failures stand out.

goals.title: Open a representative trace
goals.concept: A trace reconstructs one end-to-end request across transactions and spans.
goals.reasoning: The trace makes timing and propagation relationships explicit.
goals.evidence: The representative trace contains the scenario signal.

demonstration.narration: I'll open one trace from that group to see where the delay or error starts along a single request.
demonstration.reasoning: Aggregated percentiles and error rates cannot show where time was spent or how failure propagated. A trace shows each operation in order.
demonstration.evidence: The trace waterfall now shows the request path and its timing or error markers. Inspect the decisive detail before attributing the cause.

hints: Move from the transaction group to one request.
Choose a representative sample; Show me can demonstrate it.

goals.title: Inspect the decisive trace detail
goals.concept: Span, error, dependency, and correlated-log details explain where the symptom originated.
goals.narration: Follow the slow or failing path to the element where it starts, and inspect it.
goals.reasoning: The decisive detail distinguishes origin from upstream impact.
goals.evidence: The selected detail corroborates the finding.

demonstration.narration: I'll inspect ${var.inspect_label} to see what happened there and whether it explains the reported request problem.
demonstration.reasoning: A slow or failed upstream transaction can be impact rather than origin. The detail helps separate the originating operation from downstream symptoms.
demonstration.evidence:
The selected detail should corroborate the trace-level signal and explain why ${truth.finding} occurred.

Together, the topology and detail support the conclusion: ${truth.conclusion}

hints: Follow the slow or failed path to its deepest decisive element.
Inspect a span, error marker, or correlated log along that path.
Use ${var.inspect_label}; Show me can open it.

goals.title: Submit a trace-supported conclusion
goals.concept: Separate the originating operation from the services where its impact becomes visible.
goals.narration: Record the finding, scope, and trace evidence.
goals.reasoning: A trace-backed conclusion should identify both cause and propagation.
goals.evidence: The answer cites the representative path and detail.
hints: State where the issue starts and how it affects the request.
Use the coach's answer form: where it starts, the path it affects, and what the trace shows.
Submit the finding, scope and conclusion; Show me shows the reference summary.
